reader.requirement: At --std 85, when a USE statement names file-name-1 explicitly, only that declarative is selected for the file's I-O conditions; an INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O/EXTEND declarative never also runs for it.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectLevel >= 2002 adds the SORT GR17 return filter around the declarative's run; below 2002 a plain try/finally. Selection is not affected

reader.edition-search: grep Edition/DialectLevel/DialectBehavior in UseTierEmitter.cs (none; its remarks record the tiers as edition-invariant by determination) and DispatchEmitter.cs (one hit, above)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is one relative-file case; not exercised: an OPEN failing on a file that has both a file-name USE and a USE of the mode it is being opened in

probes.printed: 1 OPEN INPUT RA (absent): '  U-RA 35' only; 10 OPEN INPUT RA again: '  U-RA 35' only, while USE ON INPUT exists
probes.expected: only the file-name declarative runs for RA

probes.printed: 2 OPEN INPUT RB (absent): '  U-IN 35 35' (RB has no file-name USE)
probes.expected: the INPUT declarative runs for a file no USE names

citations.check: OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR4  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4

reader.notes: EmitScopeTiers emits the file-name switch first and each case ends the selection, so the mode tier is never reached for a named file. Probed with a relative file failing OPEN INPUT under both a USE ON file and a USE ON INPUT. A GLOBAL USE across nested programs was not probed (that is the inter-program module's rule).

refuter.evidence: Read UseTierEmitter.EmitScopeTiers (file-name switch first, mode tier only for files no case named) and FileConnector.UseModeView. Probe r5_use.cob at --std 85 (runs/r5_use-001), relative dynamic file RA with its own USE plus USE ON INPUT/OUTPUT/I-O: OPEN I-O RA twice -> only '  U-RA 41'; READ key 5 with no phrase -> only '  U-RA 23' (the I-O declarative did not also run). The nested-program angle (an inner USE ON INPUT against an outer USE naming the file) is governed by §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1a, which picks the declarative of the program containing the statement first, so it is no counter-case. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VIII.4.8.4 GR4  (4.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR4'; 'OK  §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1a  (║5.5.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR1a'.
